newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Hutchison out of Brazil cellular group.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison out of Brazil cellular group.

text.p: Hutchison Telecommunications, a unit of Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, and two Brazilian partners said they will not be bidding as a group to run cellular telephone services in Brazil.

The companies said in a statement that the decision was taken because Hutchison and Brazilian firm Teldin, a unit of electronics manufacturer Grupo Evadin, and investment bank Garantia have different views of the business.
Hutchison will bid on its own to run Brazil's so-called B Band cellular telephone concessions, the statement said.
Brazil's sale of B Band concessions, the first big step in the privatization of the country's telecommunications industry, is expected to begin in April.

Winners of the concessions will compete against regional subsidiaries of state holding Telebras, which currently operate on an A Band but whose operations are also expected to be turned over to private capital in the future.
